title: perf(canary): add automated detection for latency/throughput regressions and rollout guards
author: Maya Thompson
description: Context: We currently run performance canaries for model rollouts but detection is manual and the rollout logic is fragile to small latency/throughput regressions. This PR implements an automated detector and a policy-driven rollout guard to pause or rollback canary traffic when regressions are detected. Motivation: reduce time-to-detect perf regressions, avoid user-facing latency spikes during rollouts, and provide clear operational controls (hysteresis, KV-aware checks) that SRE and runtime teams can tune. What this change does: 1) Adds a continuous detector that consumes canary metrics (p95 latency, p99 latency, throughput, error-rate, kv-cache-hit-rate) and computes regression scores using baseline windows and configurable hysteresis. 2) Introduces a rollout_guard service that enforces policy decisions: pause, throttle, auto-rollback, or alert. 3) Exposes configuration via configs/perf_canary.yaml with per-model thresholds and sensitivity profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive). 4) Integrates with alerts and the canary orchestration to automatically drain canary traffic and mark the rollout failed when guard action is triggered. 5) Adds unit and end-to-end tests, CI job, and runbook docs. Implementation notes: detector supports multiple aggregation windows (1m/5m/15m), uses baseline percentiles with bootstrapped confidence intervals to reduce false positives, and is KV-cache-aware: it slices metrics by cache-hit buckets so model warmup doesn't trigger regressions. Rollout guard supports hysteresis (recover only after sustained improvement) and a grace period to allow transient noise. Security/ops: guard actions are logged to audit stream and the private control plane; actions require an allowlist for auto-rollback in Dedicated deployments. Rollout plan: feature is behind a runtime flag (perf_canary.autodetect=true) and default profile is conservative. We'll enable on internal canaries for 48h, then expand to low-traffic customer canaries after manual verification. Testing: local unit tests added, integration e2e against a canary harness, and a canary-smoke CI job that simulates regressions and verifies guard responses. Backwards compatibility: the config is additive and disabled by default. Related: ENG-4021, SRE-129, SUP-881. Checklist: [x] detector implementation [x] rollout guard engine [x] config schema and defaults [x] unit tests [x] e2e tests and CI job [x] docs (runbook + config examples) [x] canary smoke job
